newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Thursday on uncertain short-term market trend, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,418 yuan ($412) per tonne, rising 32 yuan. It opened at 3,390 and hit a low of 3,382 yuan per tonne.
May fell 120 to 3,380, July rose nine to 3,395, November put on 29 to 3,415 and the January 1998 contract fell 35 to 3,375.
Combined volume fell to 16,200 tonnes from 18,200 tonnes.
Soybean opened mixed and moved around the 3,400 yuan level for most of the session.
Traders said investors were mixed about short-term market trend and liquidation dominated the day's trade.

"It was the lack of market-moving news that kept soybeans around 3,400 yuan," one trader said. "Most investors have traded only for quick profits in recent days and they are eager to liquidate their positions once they see they can make some money."
Traders said the slow trend would persist as money continues to flow towards the more active domestic stock markets.
They said they expected soybean futures to move around current levels over the next few days. ($1=8.2951 yuan)
